newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Air NZ says to make 396 staff redundant.
newsitem.headline: Air NZ says to make 396 staff redundant.

text.p: Air New Zealand said on Thursday 396 permanent staff in its catering operations at Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch are to be made redundant.
Air NZ said it had offered staff in its catering unit a voluntary reduction package as it moved to conclude the sale of the operation to a new owner.
It said 72 percent of the staff voted to accept the package.

Air NZ said it had undertaken to provide its catering staff with a minimum of six weeks notice of redundancy, and had advised that it would be between eight and 12 weeks before new owners took over the catering operation and redundant staff were released.
The identity of the new owners would be announced shortly.
The airline has also not yet disclosed the sale price of its catering unit.

Air NZ spokesman David Beatson told Reuters there would not be any further redundancies in connection with the catering unit transaction, but the carrier was looking at improving efficiencies in other areas.

"In terms of other redundancies, we're continuing to work our way through a whole corporate-wide programme of reviewing all functions in the airline to determine if we can do things more efficiently," Beatson said.
"But there is nothing of this scale (the 396 redundancies) in contemplation anywhere else in the company."
